note: Verifies which navigation events each engine fires and what each history API can read — not timing. No statistical distribution applies: event firing is a deterministic boolean per trigger, and stack readouts are deterministic per engine build. Source of truth: probe-result.json (per-engine) and router-check.json (npm dist grep).

observation_matrix.question: For 11 navigation triggers, which triggers does each API observe?
observation_matrix.engines_agree: chromium 147.0.7727.15 and firefox 148.0.2 produced identical results

history_api_saw.note: popstate does NOT fire on pushState/replaceState, on programmatic navigation, on same-origin link clicks, on GET form submit, on location.assign(), or on cross-origin/download navigations.

navigation_api_saw.note: The navigate event fires for every trigger, with navigationType (push/replace/traverse) and canIntercept exposed.

stack_visibility.question: After 3 pushState calls in a clean context, what can each API tell you about session history?
stack_visibility.history_api: Only history.length — a single integer, and engines even disagree on it (chromium 5, firefox 4). No way to read the URL list or inspect a non-current entry.
stack_visibility.navigation_api: navigation.entries() returns the full URL array (/demo.html, ?a=1, ?b=2, ?c=3) plus currentEntry.index (3) on chromium and firefox. Absent on webkit.

spa_intercept_verified.claim: A navigate + intercept() handler renders a new view and updates the URL with zero framework — SPA routing from one event listener.
spa_intercept_verified.observed: handler_ran=true, full_page_reload_avoided=true, #outlet text replaced and URL updated to ?p=1

webkit_absence.observed: Playwright WebKit 26.4 exposes no window.navigation at all (entries, navigate, traverseTo, NavigateEvent all false). The navigate event fired 0 times; only fragment and Back were observed there via popstate/hashchange.
webkit_absence.caveat: This is a real observation about the Playwright WebKit build, NOT a verdict on Safari. Playwright's WebKit != Safari; caniuse lists Safari 26.2+ as supporting the API and we did NOT measure real Safari. Practical implication: teams running Playwright WebKit E2E will see a Navigation-API router silently fall back there.

router_adoption.question: Do the mainstream React routers use the Navigation API yet?
router_adoption.method: npm pack the published packages, extract, grep shipped dist for window.navigation / NavigateEvent, and for popstate.
router_adoption.conclusion: As of 2026-07-24, neither shipped package references the Navigation API; both still listen to popstate and call pushState.

not_measured.real_safari: Playwright WebKit != Safari. Safari behavior is cited, never presented as firsthand.
not_measured.real_user_browsers: Headless automation only. Extensions, restored sessions, and bfcache may behave differently.
not_measured.unmeasured_surfaces: scroll/focus restoration, bfcache, intercept() precommitHandler/commit options, POST forms, and traverseTo() in real use were not exercised.
not_measured.history_length_discrepancy: history.length split 5 (chromium) vs 4 (firefox); likely initial about:blank counting, root cause not investigated.
not_measured.router_grep_scope: Published dist only. Unreleased branches, experimental flags, and open PRs were not inspected.

cited_not_measured.claim: Navigation API reached Baseline 'newly available' in January 2026.
Support: Chrome/Edge 102+, Firefox 147+, Safari desktop/iOS 26.2+; global coverage ~87.37%.
